about: The first prayer of the Canon. Through Jesus Christ, the priest asks the Father to accept the offerings and to grant the Church peace, protection, unity and governance. The missal leaves a slot here for the reigning Pope and the local bishop, named with all who keep the Catholic faith.

seg.nr: After the Preface the priest spreads his hands, raises them slightly and joins them, lifts his eyes to heaven and lowers them at once, then bows low before the altar and rests his hands upon it.

seg.tr: Therefore, most merciful Father, through Jesus Christ, Your Son, our Lord, we humbly pray and beseech You

fn.w001: Accusative object of “rogámus” (w013) and “pétimus” (w015), placed at the prayer's beginning.
fn.w002: Connects this prayer with the preceding liturgy: “therefore”.
fn.w003: A superlative in the vocative, sharing its case with “Pater” (w004).
fn.w004: Vocative. “Te” (w001), “rogámus” (w013) and “pétimus” (w015) are addressed to the Father.
fn.w008: In apposition to “Christum” (w007), and so accusative.
fn.w012: A nominative plural adjective referring to the unstated “we”: “we, the suppliants”.

seg.nr: The priest kisses the altar and joins his hands before his breast.

fn.w016: An older form of ut. Not the infinitive of utor (to use), though it is spelt the same.
fn.w017: In the phrase “accépta habére”: “to regard as accepted”. It agrees with “dona” (w022), “múnera” (w024) and “sacrifícia” (w027).

seg.nr: The priest makes three signs of the cross over the Host and the chalice together.

seg.tr: these gifts, these offerings, these holy and undefiled sacrifices,

fn.w021: The first of three occurrences of “hæc” at which the priest signs the cross over the Host and chalice.

seg.nr: The priest spreads his hands and goes on.

seg.tr: We offer them to You above all for Your holy Catholic Church. Graciously grant her peace, preserve her, unite her, and govern her throughout the world,

fn.w030: In primis is a fixed adverbial phrase meaning “first of all”. No gender is therefore assigned here.
fn.w031: An accusative neuter plural relative referring to “dona” (w022), “múnera” (w024) and “sacrifícia” (w027).
fn.w039: Feminine accusative singular, referring to “Ecclésia” (w035). It is the object of the following four infinitives.
fn.w045: “Dignéris” governs the four infinitives that precede it.
fn.w046: It agrees with “orbe” (w047). The phrase “toto orbe terrárum” expresses place without the preposition in.
fn.w048: A genitive plural depending on “orbe” (w047). The whole phrase means the whole world.

seg.tr: with Your servant, our Pope, our Bishop, and all who uphold the true Catholic and Apostolic faith.

fn.w049: An adverb in the phrase “una cum”: together with.
fn.w056: An ablative after “cum” (w050). Here it is a title for the local bishop.
fn.w057: It agrees with “Antístite” (w056). The missal provides for the local bishop's name here.
fn.w060: With “ómnibus” (w059), it forms an ablative plural phrase: with all the orthodox.
fn.w066: An ablative plural after “una” (w049) and “cum” (w050). With “fídei” (w065): those who profess the faith.
